official_reference_document_set.note: Gusto publishes one Markdown-wrapped OpenAPI fragment per App Integrations endpoint. Each raw page and extracted OpenAPI fragment is independently hashed below.

supplemental_pins.purpose: product boundary, production pre-approval, security review, and demo-only testing
company OAuth access tokens and production versus demo origins
system-token isolation and short-lived bearer placement
date-version request header and deprecation behavior
200 requests per minute per OAuth grant
structured non-2xx errors array and categories

official_inbound_webhook_events.note: These guides document payloads Gusto sends to subscribers. They are provenance only and are not emitted as outbound callable operations.

transport.company_auth: OAuth2 bearer scoped to exactly one company; access and single-use refresh tokens are connection-owned.
transport.system_auth: Separate two-hour SystemAccess bearer for provisioning, events, and webhook administration; manually enrolled because the connection auth union has no client-credentials grant.

contract_gaps.product_boundary: The source index also contains a much larger Gusto Embedded Payroll product. This family is deliberately and exclusively the App Integrations API; mixing products would overstate production entitlements and token authority.
contract_gaps.split_openapi_fragments: Each reference page embeds only its own OpenAPI path and shared components. No single official fetchable OpenAPI document covers the complete App Integrations surface.
contract_gaps.demo_vs_production: Official endpoint fragments name https://api.gusto-demo.com; the authentication guide proves https://api.gusto.com after Gusto QA. Packs use the production origin and retain both facts in the fixture.
contract_gaps.credential_lifecycle: POST /oauth/token and POST /oauth/revoke are excluded so client secrets, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and revocation remain connection-owned.
contract_gaps.dual_token_contexts: CompanyAccessAuth and SystemAccessAuth are not interchangeable. Six leaves use per-company OAuth; the system leaf uses a separately enrolled bearer and no bundled recipe crosses the boundary.
contract_gaps.system_token_expiry: System access tokens expire after two hours. The generic connection contract has no client-credentials refresh mode, so the system leaf documents manual bearer renewal instead of claiming durable automatic authentication.
contract_gaps.production_access: Gusto production access is partner-gated by pre-approval, a security review, QA, and per-use-case scopes. Demo success does not imply production authorization.
contract_gaps.response_header_pagination: GET /v1/events returns X-Has-Next-Page and accepts starting_after_uuid, but the gateway cannot inspect that custom header or derive a cursor from a root array. Explicit cursor inputs remain available; no automatic completeness claim is made.
contract_gaps.explicit_null_requests: Any request contract with a nullable top-level property uses body_raw because the REST top-level body projection drops null-valued body.* arguments. Root unions, free-form maps, nested int64 values, and required all-optional bodies use the same fail-closed route.
contract_gaps.errors: Gusto failures are non-2xx responses with structured errors[] entries. The HTTP adapter surfaces them as step failures; response schemas model successful bodies rather than inventing a 200 business-error union.
contract_gaps.scopes: All 134 admitted operations whose pages declare scopes carry exact required_scopes metadata. Token introspection is the only admitted page without a documented scope.
contract_gaps.source_eligibility: The App Integrations surface has no honest task, note, or project entity. Adjacent payroll and HR objects are not semantically relabeled, so no work-entity Source is declared.

source_eligibility.evidence: No App Integrations operation returns a task entity; time sheets, notifications, and webhook events are not relabeled as tasks.
No App Integrations operation returns a durable user-authored note entity.
Departments, companies, payrolls, and reports are not semantically project entities and are not relabeled.
